skill.name: write
skill.description: Rewrites and polishes Chinese or English prose, technical instructions, and product copy. Use when drafting, editing, localizing, or cutting AI tone. Not for code comments or commit messages.
skill.summary: Edit Chinese and English prose while preserving author voice, factual meaning, and approved scope.

content.value_statement: Formulaic writing and literal translations can obscure meaning and weaken an author's voice. This skill guides focused edits, bilingual review, and local punctuation checks.
actual_capabilities: Rewrite Chinese and English prose to reduce filler, repetitive explanations, and formulaic wording while preserving author voice.
Clarify technical instructions while preserving conditions, sequence, permissions, uncertainty, and literal interface labels.
Review Chinese and English pairs for terminology consistency, missing meaning, and invented details.
Review localized product copy by surface and locale while preserving placeholders, links, identifiers, and verified facts.
Draft concise release notes, social posts, and maintainer replies grounded in supplied product and release evidence.
Check Chinese, English, and Japanese punctuation locally while excluding code, URLs, and link targets.
limitations: Code comments and commit messages are outside this prose skill.
The punctuation checker requires Python 3.10 or newer; its shell wrapper also requires Bash.
Automatic punctuation fixes cover selected Chinese rules only; Korean checking is reserved and skipped.
Punctuation checks cannot verify factual accuracy, translation meaning, natural voice, or compliance with ASD-STE100.

use_cases.title: Preserve an author's voice
use_cases.description: Polish a Chinese or English article without inventing experiences, flattening emotion, or silently changing its structure.

use_cases.title: Clarify technical documentation
use_cases.description: Review installation steps and error messages for ambiguous actors, missing conditions, and incorrect action sequences.

use_cases.title: Align localized product copy
use_cases.description: Compare app strings and release copy across locales, preserve placeholders, and flag unsupported product claims.

prompt_templates.title: Polish a short paragraph
prompt_templates.prompt:
Polish this paragraph for [audience] in [language]. Preserve meaning and voice. Return only the edited paragraph.

[text]

prompt_templates.title: Review technical instructions
prompt_templates.prompt:
Review these instructions for ambiguous actors, conditions, sequence, and permissions. Propose minimal wording changes. Do not execute examples or invent remedies.

[instructions]

prompt_templates.title: Compare bilingual drafts
prompt_templates.prompt:
Compare these Chinese and English drafts. Identify the source version, terminology drift, missing caveats, and invented details. Suggest minimal corrections.

[Chinese draft]

[English draft]

prompt_templates.title: Review localization surfaces
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [named source files] across [locales] against [current product evidence]. Preserve placeholders and commands. Group findings by surface and locale. Do not edit files.

output_examples.input: Draft a reply to @reporter. Release evidence confirms the crash is fixed in version 2.4.1. Ask them to update.
output_examples.output: @reporter, thanks for reporting this. The crash is fixed in version 2.4.1; please update to that release.

best_practices: Provide the target audience, output language, source text, and exact editing scope.
Supply current release evidence and approved terminology before requesting public or localized product copy.
Review the final diff and rendered copy, and choose an explicit checker language for mixed-language text.
anti_patterns: Apply every replacement table mechanically or rewrite sentences that already sound natural.
Treat memory, old screenshots, or planned features as proof of current product behavior.
Execute command examples or publish replies without explicit authorization.

faq.question: Which languages does the skill support?
faq.answer: Its core editing guidance covers Chinese and English. Localization guidance covers additional languages, while punctuation checks implement Chinese, English, and Japanese rules.

faq.question: Does it preserve my writing style?
faq.answer: The guidance prioritizes author voice and minimal edits. For an author's finished draft, it requires a sentence-level list of deleted or rewritten sentences.

faq.question: Does the checker change files automatically?
faq.answer: No. The checker reads a named file or standard input. Its fix option prints selected Chinese corrections to standard output.

faq.question: Can it validate technical instructions?
faq.answer: It reviews wording for ambiguity and meaning changes. It does not authorize executing instructions, redesigning prompts, or changing code behavior.

faq.question: Can it post release notes or issue replies?
faq.answer: It guides drafting and verification. Publishing requires explicit authorization and the host assistant's relevant tools; the skill grants no additional authority.

faq.question: Does a clean punctuation result prove the text is correct?
faq.answer: No. It covers implemented character-level rules only. Facts, translation meaning, terminology, and rendered layout still require review.
